title: Parashurama's Challenge
captions: After the weddings, Vishvamitra blessed everyone and left for the northern mountains. King Janaka gave his daughters many gifts, and King Dasharatha set out for Ayodhya with his family.
On the road, birds began to cry out in fear, but gentle deer walked calmly around the king. “Danger is coming,” said Vasishtha, “but the deer tell us it will pass. Do not be afraid.”
Suddenly a fierce wind began to blow. The earth shook, trees crashed down and dust hid the sun. Everyone in the king's army stood still, unable to see the way.
Out of the darkness came Parashurama, the great sage, son of Jamadagni. He blazed like fire, with an axe on his shoulder and a mighty bow in his hand. Vasishtha welcomed him with water.
“Rama, I have heard that you broke Lord Shiva's bow,” said Parashurama. “Now string this bow of Lord Vishnu and fit an arrow. Then we shall fight!” King Dasharatha begged him to spare his son.
Rama had listened quietly, out of respect for his father. Now he took the bow and strung it with ease. “You are a brahmana and family to my guru Vishvamitra,” he said, “so I will not harm you.”

“But this arrow must strike something,” said Rama. Parashurama knew then that Rama was Lord Vishnu himself. He let the arrow take away the heavenly worlds he had won by tapas, honoured Rama and left for Mount Mahendra.
story: After the weddings, Vishvamitra blessed everyone and left for the northern mountains. King Janaka gave his daughters many gifts, and King Dasharatha set out for Ayodhya with his whole family.
On the road, strange signs appeared. Birds cried out in fear, but gentle deer walked calmly around the king. Vasishtha explained that danger was coming, but the calm deer showed that it would pass.

Suddenly a fierce wind blew. The earth shook, trees crashed down and dust hid the sun. Out of the darkness came Parashurama, the great sage and son of Jamadagni. He blazed like fire, with an axe on his shoulder and a mighty bow in his hand. Vasishtha welcomed him with water.

Parashurama had heard that Rama broke Lord Shiva's bow. He held out the bow of Lord Vishnu and challenged Rama to string it, fit an arrow and then fight him. King Dasharatha begged him to spare his son.

Rama had listened quietly, out of respect for his father. Now he took the bow and strung it with ease. He said he would not harm Parashurama, a brahmana and family to his guru Vishvamitra, but the arrow must strike something. Parashurama understood then that Rama was Lord Vishnu himself. He let the arrow take away the heavenly worlds he had won by tapas, honoured Rama and left for Mount Mahendra.
lesson: When Parashurama arrived like a storm and challenged him, Rama did not shout back or boast. He listened quietly out of respect for his father, and when it was time to act, he acted with steady hands and chose not to harm the great sage. In our tradition, Shanti means peace inside us, and our elders teach that a calm mind sees clearly even when others are upset. Because Rama stayed calm, the danger passed, and Parashurama went on his way in peace.
lesson_long: Shanti means peace: a quiet, steady calm inside us.

Parashurama arrived like a storm, angry and challenging. Rama did not shout back or boast. He waited respectfully while his father spoke, and when it was time to act, he acted with steady hands. He even chose not to harm the great sage.
Our elders teach that a calm mind sees clearly, even when others are upset. Because Rama stayed calm, the danger passed and everyone went on their way in peace.
tradition: Many Hindu prayers end with the words Om Shanti Shanti Shanti. Peace is asked for three times: peace within us, peace in the world around us, and peace from forces beyond our control.

Parashurama is the sixth avatar of Lord Vishnu, and Rama is the seventh. In this meeting, one avatar makes way for the next. Parashurama is honoured as a chiranjivi, one who lives on through the ages, and is believed to still do tapas on Mount Mahendra.
words: the sixth avatar of Lord Vishnu
one who lives on through the ages
a form in which God comes into the world
the sacred sound at the start and end of prayers
question: When someone around you is upset or angry, what helps you stay calm?
questions: When someone around you is upset or angry, what helps you stay calm?
How did the calm deer help the travellers feel less afraid?

card_lesson: When Parashurama challenged him, Rama did not shout or boast. He stayed calm, acted with steady hands and chose not to harm anyone. Shanti means keeping peace inside us.
